narrative:
The model predicts a 13% chance that you will fail your final year, which indicates that while there is a possibility of passing, the likelihood of needing to take remedial courses is significant. This prediction is based on several factors that have been identified as influential in determining student success.

One of the most important factors is your study time. The model suggests that you are currently studying less than two hours a week, which is notably lower than many of your peers who passed, where over half study between two to five hours. This lower study time may not be sufficient to grasp the material needed for success.

Another key factor is your aspirations for higher education. While this is a positive indicator, it alone does not guarantee success. The model indicates that your motivation must be matched with adequate preparation and study habits.

Lastly, your record of past failures is a strong positive influence on the prediction of failure. Although you have not had any past class failures, the model suggests that without consistent study habits and support, the risk of not passing increases.

To improve your academic performance, consider increasing your study time and seeking additional educational support. Engaging more actively with your studies and possibly participating in extra classes could help reinforce your understanding of the material. Additionally, maintaining a balance between your social life and academic responsibilities will be crucial as you work towards your goals.
